# Avijjānīvaraṇa Sutta (Iti 14 (It 1.14 PTS It 7))

**ID:** Iti 14 (It 1.14 PTS It 7)
**Section:** Itivuttaka (iti)
**Collection:** Sutta
**Title (Pali):** Avijjānīvaraṇa Sutta
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0504m.mul0.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Avijjānīvaraṇa Sutta* (*Itivuttaka* 14; PTS It 7) is a short discourse from the first division of the *Itivuttaka*. In this sutta, the Buddha asserts that he perceives no single hindrance other than ignorance (*avijjānīvaraṇa*) by which beings are so obstructed that they wander and transmigrate through *saṁsāra* for an immense period of time [Webster 2005]. Paired closely with the subsequent *Taṇhāsaṁyojana Sutta* (Iti 15), it highlights ignorance and craving as the primary impediments to human liberation and spiritual progress [Webster 2005].
